expected_headings.text: List of Nobel laureates in Physics (excerpt)

expected_tables.location: single table spanning the whole document body
expected_tables.notes: Genuine class='wikitable' (bordered) table. Header row uses rowspan=2 on 'Year', 'Country', 'Citation', and 'Reference(s)' columns (these headers span both header sub-rows vertically since there's a second header sub-row for 'Image'/'Name'), and colspan=2 on 'Laureate' (splitting into 'Image' and 'Name' sub-columns beneath it). Body rows also use rowspan on the 'Year' cell for years with multiple co-laureates (shared prize), and some Country/Citation cells span multiple laureate rows within the same year. Verified directly: 19 rowspan attributes + 18 colspan attributes present across the excerpt (41 <tr> rows total including header).

math_notes: No mathematical notation in this excerpt (physics laureate names/citations are prose, not equations).
expected_noise_elements: Wikipedia citation/reference superscript markers (<sup class='mw-ref'>) embedded inside header and body cells
notes_for_implementer: This is the primary 'legitimate complex table' fixture -- unlike fixtures 05/06 (false-positive navbox tables) and fixture 04 (false-positive OCR noise), this table IS real tabular data and SHOULD be detected and reconstructed faithfully, including the two-level header (rowspan+colspan combination) and the in-body rowspans for shared-year/shared-country cells. A good normalization should either (a) faithfully reproduce the merged-cell structure in the output markdown/table representation, or (b) explicitly and correctly flatten it (e.g. repeating the spanned value into each logical row/column) rather than silently dropping cells or misaligning columns after the first rowspan is encountered. This is the positive control to pair against the false-positive fixtures: Pith must find exactly ONE table here, matching its true row/column footprint, not zero and not multiple fragments.
